correctness.rationale: All codimension-one partial transversals have exactly two allowed top completions, of sums zero and one. Their oriented incidence coefficients at the common deleted coordinate have the same sign, so any integral top cycle alternates coefficients across the bipartite top-facet adjacency graph. Two-step moves +e_i−e_j generate every vector of sum zero in (Z/q)^n even for composite q, proving graph connectivity and top kernel generated by (+1 on sum0, −1 on sum1). The full colorful join J has only top reduced integral homology Z^((q−1)^n); the pair (J,K) has relative free chain group of rank (q−2)q^(n−1) solely in degree n−1. The long exact sequence yields rank of lower homology and vanishing elsewhere. Repeating over every prime and applying universal coefficients rules out all torsion. Independent full simplicial boundary reductions over F2/F3/F5 gave top rank one and lower ranks 0 at (n,q)=(2,2), 2 at (3,3), 6 at (3,4), 12 at (4,3); these finite verifications are corroborative only. For q=2 the subcomplex equals the full join, so lower rank vanishes; for n=2 H~_0=0; for n,q≥3 the lower rank is strictly positive.

originality.rationale: Ayzenberg–Khoroshavkina’s 2026 generalized-inflation flabbiness theorem assumes global completion/flabbiness. The present q>2 family contains every partial colorful assignment but excludes q−2 full transversal sum classes, so the flabby hypothesis does not apply and its wedge theorem does not determine this homology. A single modular-sum Latin hypercube layer has no top class; putting two adjacent layers together produces a connected bipartite facet-incidence graph and creates Z in top degree while leaving an adjacent lower free group. No cited broader general classification with these exact two-layer Betti numbers was found. The method uses standard joins and long exact sequence, which are credited.
